newsitem.title: GREECE: ABC FACTORS SAYS JAN-MAY PROFIT UP 80PCT TO 350MLN DRS.
newsitem.headline: ABC FACTORS SAYS JAN-MAY PROFIT UP 80PCT TO 350MLN DRS.

text.p: ABC Factors, a joint venture of Bank of Cyrpus and Alpha Credit Bank, saw its operating profits rise 80 percent to 350 million drachmas in the first five months of 1997 compared to the same period in 1996, it said in a statement.
ABC Factors was the first company to offer factoring services to the local market.
Its turnover jumped 71 percent year-on-year to 38 billion drachmas in the first five months of the year and is expected to reach 100 billion drachmas in 1997, it said in a statement.
ABC Factors cooperates with 150 local firms and manages the receivables of 6,000 companies throughout Greece, it added.
"To help factoring grow further in Greece, ABC factors reduced the interest it charges to 17.25 percent from 14.25 percent," it said.
The interest rate is not burdened with the EFTE tax and the contribution of Law 128, it said.
